label: CER eCTD 4.0 — State of the Art
description: State-of-the-art review for IVC filter technology supporting VenaGuard™ CER.

inputs.device_name: VenaGuard™ Retrievable Inferior Vena Cava (IVC) Filter
inputs.medical_condition: Deep Vein Thrombosis (DVT) complicated by contraindications to or failure of anticoagulation therapy, with risk of pulmonary embolism (PE)
inputs.epidemiology: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) — comprising DVT and PE — affects approximately 1–2 per 1,000 adults annually in Europe. PE is the third most common cardiovascular cause of death after myocardial infarction and stroke, accounting for an estimated 300,000–500,000 deaths annually in the EU. Approximately 2–5% of DVT patients have absolute contraindications to anticoagulation, and an additional 3–8% experience anticoagulation failure, representing the target population for IVC filter placement.
inputs.disease_natural_history: Without treatment, proximal DVT carries a 40–50% risk of PE within 3 months. Fatal PE occurs in 1–5% of untreated DVT cases. Patients with contraindications to anticoagulation (active bleeding, recent major surgery, hemorrhagic stroke, severe thrombocytopenia) face the highest PE risk with the fewest treatment options.
inputs.current_treatment_landscape: First-line therapy for VTE is systemic anticoagulation (LMWH, DOACs, warfarin). When anticoagulation is contraindicated or has failed, mechanical thromboprophylaxis with IVC filters is the standard of care per ESC 2019, ACCP, and SIR guidelines. Catheter-directed thrombolysis and surgical thrombectomy are alternatives in specific clinical scenarios but do not substitute for long-term PE prevention.
inputs.alternative_devices: Marketed retrievable IVC filters include: (1) Bard G2 Express (C.R. Bard/BD) — market leader, conical design, 8.5F delivery; (2) Cook Celect Platinum (Cook Medical) — tulip-shaped, 8.5F; (3) Optease (Cordis/Cardinal Health) — symmetrical, non-conical; (4) Denali (Bard/BD) — newer-generation, conical, 7F; (5) ALN Optional Filter (ALN Implants) — EU-marketed, retrievable up to 12 months. Permanent (non-retrievable) filters include: Greenfield stainless steel filter, TrapEase, and Bird's Nest filter — use declining due to push toward retrievability.
inputs.unmet_clinical_needs: Key unmet needs in the IVC filter market include: (1) Higher retrieval success rates — current market average 80–93%, with failed retrieval resulting in permanent implantation; (2) Lower fracture rates — strut fracture is a known long-term complication, reported at 1–12% depending on filter type; (3) Lower-profile delivery — smaller access site reduces bleeding and enables outpatient procedures; (4) Longer retrieval window — many filters become incorporated or tilted after 3–6 months, limiting retrievability; (5) Better long-term data on permanent implantation outcomes.
inputs.applicable_standards: ISO 14708-7 (implantable IVC filters); ISO 14155:2020 (clinical investigations); ISO 14971:2019 (risk management); ISO 10993 series (biocompatibility); EU MDR 2017/745 Annex I GSPRs; MEDDEV 2.7/1 rev. 4 (clinical evaluation); IEC 62366-1:2015 (usability); EN ISO 11607 (packaging); ASTM F2063 (nitinol standard)
inputs.relevant_guidelines: ESC 2019 Guidelines on PE (IVC filter recommendation: Class IIb, Level C); ACCP 2016 Antithrombotic Therapy guidelines; SIR 2020 Reporting Standards for IVC Filter Placement and Retrieval; ACR Appropriateness Criteria for IVC filter placement; FDA 2014 Safety Communication on retrievable IVC filters (recommending retrieval when PE risk subsides)
inputs.harmonized_standards: EN ISO 14708-7, EN ISO 14971, EN ISO 10993-1, EN ISO 14155, EN IEC 62366-1
inputs.common_specifications: No EU Common Specifications (CS) currently published for IVC filters under EU MDR Article 9.
inputs.technology_evolution: IVC filter technology has evolved from permanent stainless steel filters (1960s–1980s) to retrievable nitinol designs (2000s–present). Key advances include: shape-memory nitinol alloys enabling retrieval, lower-profile delivery systems (from 12F to 7F), improved strut geometry reducing migration and tilting, and enhanced fatigue resistance reducing fracture rates. The trend is toward optional/retrievable filters with shorter dwell times, reflecting FDA and EU guidance to retrieve filters when no longer clinically indicated.
inputs.regulatory_landscape: In the EU, IVC filters are classified as Class III under EU MDR 2017/745 (Rule 8 — implantable device). Clinical evidence requirements include: pre-clinical testing per ISO 14708-7, clinical investigation per ISO 14155, equivalence-based or direct clinical data per MEDDEV 2.7/1, and ongoing PMCF per EU MDR Article 61(11). Notified Body review is required. In the US, IVC filters are Class II (Product Code: MNS), cleared via 510(k) with predicate comparison.
